title: Seller Reinstatement Eligibility Under Revised Strike Policy with Temporal Overlap
scenario_text:
**Zendesk — Ticket #ZD-438901 (UrbanEdge, Jun 10, 2026)**
Subject: 'Reinstatement Request — CedarWood Artisans'
From: mark.ellison@cedarwoodartisans.com
Body: 'Requesting reinstatement per your updated marketplace policy communications. Our store was suspended September 2025 under the 3-strike policy. We've resolved the counterfeit complaint (supplier misunderstanding) and have had no activity on any Atlas platform since. Please review.'
Agent note: 'Routed to T&S for reinstatement review per SOP. Account was suspended under Policy v2.1.'

**Shopify Plus — Seller Portal (Brand: UrbanEdge) [ARCHIVED]**
Store: CedarWood Artisans | Owner: Mark Ellison | Status: SUSPENDED (Sep 22, 2025)
Strike history:
- Strike 1 (Mar 2025): Late shipment rate >8% over 30 days
- Strike 2 (Jul 2025): Counterfeit claim from brand owner (DMCA notice, Nike)
- Strike 3 (Sep 2025): Second counterfeit claim (DMCA notice, Patagonia) — automatic suspension triggered
Chargeback ratio at suspension: 0.9% (within threshold)

**Google Doc — 'Marketplace Seller Enforcement Policy v3.0' (Effective May 1, 2026)**
Section 6.1 — Reinstatement Eligibility:
'Sellers suspended under prior policy versions may apply for reinstatement if: (a) minimum 6 months have elapsed since suspension, (b) the violation type that triggered suspension is eligible for reinstatement under current policy, (c) seller has completed remediation steps outlined in their suspension notice.'
Section 3.4 — Strike Categories (v3.0):
'Category A (Operational): Late shipment, response time violations — 5-strike threshold, strikes expire after 6 months.
Category B (IP/Counterfeit): DMCA violations — 2 strikes result in 12-month suspension; reinstatement available after 12 months with brand owner confirmation of resolution.
Category C (Fraud): Chargebacks, fake reviews, identity fraud — permanent ban, no reinstatement.'

**Slack — #trust-safety (Jun 12, 2026, 9:18 AM)**
@ryan.okonma: Team — got a reinstatement request for CedarWood Artisans, suspended Sep 2025. They had 3 strikes under v2.1. Need to figure out how this maps to v3.0 categories.
@jessica.tran: Their strikes were: 1 operational (late shipments) + 2 IP/counterfeit (DMCA). Under v3.0, the operational strike wouldn't even count toward suspension — different category, higher threshold.
@ryan.okonma: Right. So effectively they have 2 Category B strikes under the new framework. What's the reinstatement window for Cat B?
@jessica.tran: 12 months from suspension date.
@ryan.okonma: That's September 2026. They're only at 9 months.
@jessica.tran: :grimacing: Yeah. Close but not there yet.
@marcus.bell: (Jun 12, 10:02 AM) Wait — didn't we decide in the enforcement committee meeting that the 6-month elapsed time in Section 6.1(a) overrides category-specific windows for sellers suspended under prior policy versions? I thought that was the whole point of the transition clause.
@ryan.okonma: :thinking_face: Was that in the meeting notes?
@marcus.bell: I don't think Rachel took notes that day. It was the May 8 meeting.
[No further replies]

**Google Calendar — 'T&S Enforcement Committee Sync' (May 8, 2026, 2:00 PM)**
Required: ryan.okonma (accepted), marcus.bell (accepted), jessica.tran (accepted), rachel.wong (accepted), vp.lossprevention (declined)
Optional: legal-marketplace (no response)
Attachment: 'Agenda - May 8 Enforcement Committee.docx' (last modified: May 7, 2026; 0 bytes — empty)
No meeting notes document linked.
question: Is CedarWood Artisans eligible for reinstatement today (June 2026), and what policy basis supports the decision?

contributor.name: Ryan Okonma
contributor.title: Marketplace Trust & Safety Lead
contributor.domain_expertise: Seller identity verification, ban evasion detection, fraud ring identification, policy enforcement across multi-brand marketplace

choices: Yes — Section 6.1(a) requires only 6 months elapsed since suspension; CedarWood was suspended September 2025, so they meet the 6-month minimum and are eligible for reinstatement pending remediation confirmation.
No — under v3.0 Category B rules, IP/counterfeit suspensions require 12 months before reinstatement; CedarWood is only at 9 months (September 2025 to June 2026) and must wait until September 2026.

No — the enforcement committee meeting had no notes, the VP Loss Prevention declined attendance, and legal did not respond; without documented approval from the committee and required stakeholders, the category-specific 12-month window in Section 3.4 applies.

Yes — the enforcement committee decided on May 8 that Section 6.1(a)'s 6-month clause overrides category-specific windows for sellers suspended under prior policies; this constitutes an approved exception even without written notes.
